- When sentiment is negative or shows early negative drift, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the next 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive but price is trending down, model underestimates downward momentum; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overestimates short-term volatility in low-sentiment periods; apply smoothing or reduce forecast variance by 15–20%.
- In high-sentiment periods with strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture the full rally; increase forecast by 2–5% in first 3–5 days of positive sentiment.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in model; if price is above 20-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Forecast horizon >14 days: model tends to underestimate downward corrections; add 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is neutral or negative.
